findings.explanation: The transfer runs on a schedule (default 'every day 02:00') with neither email_preferences nor notification_pubsub_topic set. A scheduled run that fails - bad CSV, missing objects, revoked KMS access - is recorded only in the DTS run history. Nobody is told, so the landing table silently goes stale until a consumer notices.
findings.remediation: Expose an optional notification_pubsub_topic variable and an enable_failure_email flag, and wire them into the resource.
findings.title: Data transfer config has no failure notification configured

findings.explanation: file_format = CSV and write_disposition = APPEND are baked in, and no CSV option (skip_leading_rows, field_delimiter, max_bad_records, allow_jagged_rows) is exposed. A consumer whose CSVs carry header rows cannot suppress them and will load the header as a data row; a consumer wanting JSON/AVRO/PARQUET, or MIRROR semantics so re-runs replace rather than duplicate rows, has to fork the module. Every param here is a plain string in a map, so parameterising costs nothing.
findings.remediation: Add variables for file_format (default CSV), write_disposition (default APPEND) and an extra_params map merged into params rather than hardcoding.
findings.title: Transfer params hardcode file_format and write_disposition with no CSV parsing options exposed

findings.explanation: versioning.enabled = true, but the only lifecycle_rule matches on age = 90 with no with_state, so it defaults to LIVE objects only. Noncurrent versions - one per overwrite of an incoming CSV, plus one per deletion of a live object at day 90 - are never deleted and accumulate for the life of the bucket. This is exactly the growth HLD_GCP_339 targets, and it passes here because a lifecycle rule exists at all.
findings.remediation: Add a second lifecycle_rule targeting noncurrent versions, e.g. num_newer_versions = 3 and days_since_noncurrent_time = 30 with action type Delete.
findings.title: Versioned bucket lifecycle rule does not expire noncurrent object versions

findings.explanation: GCS bucket names share one global namespace. Both example buckets hardcoded a fixed name, so the first person to apply claimed it and everyone else - including CI in a second project - got a 409 conflict. The KMS key ring is NOT affected: key ring names are scoped to project+location, so they do not collide across users, and a stable name keeps re-apply idempotent.
findings.remediation: Both bucket names are now suffixed with data.google_project.current.project_id, which is globally unique in GCP and stable across re-applies.
findings.title: Example hardcodes a globally-unique GCS bucket name

findings.explanation: The dataset, key ring, bucket and module call each carry a separate europe-west2 literal. BigQuery Data Transfer requires all of them to agree; changing region means editing four files, and a missed one fails at apply time with a location mismatch rather than at plan time.
findings.remediation: Define locals { location = "europe-west2" } once and reference local.location from all four resources.
findings.title: Region literal europe-west2 repeated across four example resources

findings.explanation: var.location defaults to europe-west2. The variable's own description says it must match the destination dataset, so a consumer whose dataset is in US and who forgets to set it gets a silent region mismatch instead of a required-variable error. A published module's defaults are the one place a wrong value escapes the consumer's review.
findings.remediation: Drop the default so location is required, since correctness depends on matching the caller's dataset location.
findings.title: Reusable module ships an organisation-specific default region

suggested_policies.rationale: Scheduled BigQuery Data Transfer configs that set neither email_preferences.enable_failure_email nor notification_pubsub_topic fail silently. Fixed resource type, two unambiguous attribute paths, fires identically on any config; no existing holden policy covers google_bigquery_data_transfer_config beyond CMEK (HLD_GCP_400).
suggested_policies.yaml:
id: HLD_GCP_XXX
name: BigQuery Data Transfer configs should notify on failure
principle: reliability
severity: LOW
rationale: |
  A scheduled transfer that fails records the failure only in the Data Transfer
  Service run history. Without a failure email or a Pub/Sub notification topic
  nobody is alerted, and the destination table silently goes stale.
remediation: |
  Set at least one notification channel:
    email_preferences {
      enable_failure_email = true
    }
  or:
    notification_pubsub_topic = google_pubsub_topic.transfer_alerts.id
resources:
  google_bigquery_data_transfer_config:
    path: notification_pubsub_topic
    not_null: true

suggested_policies.rationale: A versioned bucket whose only lifecycle rules target live objects retains every noncurrent version forever. Deterministic: versioning.enabled is true AND no lifecycle_rule condition sets num_newer_versions / days_since_noncurrent_time / with_state = ARCHIVED. Distinct from HLD_GCP_339, which passes as soon as any lifecycle rule exists.
suggested_policies.yaml:
id: HLD_GCP_XXX
name: Versioned GCS buckets should expire noncurrent object versions
principle: cost
severity: LOW
rationale: |
  With versioning enabled, every overwrite and every delete leaves a noncurrent
  version behind. A lifecycle rule with no with_state defaults to LIVE objects,
  so noncurrent versions accumulate indefinitely and are billed at full rate.
remediation: |
  Add a lifecycle rule targeting noncurrent versions:
    lifecycle_rule {
      condition {
        num_newer_versions         = 3
        days_since_noncurrent_time = 30
        with_state                 = "ARCHIVED"
      }
      action {
        type = "Delete"
      }
    }
resources:
  google_storage_bucket:
    when:
      path: versioning.enabled
      equals: true
    path: lifecycle_rule.condition.num_newer_versions
    not_null: true
